title: Umm Sulaym
hook: who accepted faith as her dowry, and bore a grief with remarkable patience (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, al-Shifa bint Abdullah, who taught Hafsah to write. Your line was: she taught writing. Who did you sit beside while they read? Day eight hundred fifty.

A man of Medina named Abu Talhah comes to ask a woman to marry him. The woman is Umm Sulaym, the mother of Anas, the boy who served the Prophet, whom we met earlier on this road. She has become Muslim. He has not. When the talk turns to a dowry, she names one, and it isn't anything he can carry in his hands. Today: Umm Sulaym, in two scenes, one at the start of a marriage and one in the middle of it.
screen: `A PROPOSAL IN MEDINA.` → `NOT GOLD.` → `TWO SCENES IN ONE MARRIAGE.`

segments.voice: The first scene is in the Sunan of al-Nasa'i. Abu Talhah proposed, and Umm Sulaym answered that a man like him was not someone to turn away, but she was a Muslim and he was not, and she could not marry him as things were. If you accept Islam, she said, that will be my dowry, and I'll ask you for nothing else. He accepted Islam, and that was her dowry. Faith for a dowry. The second scene is in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, and it is hard. Their young son was ill, and while Abu Talhah was out, the boy died. Umm Sulaym prepared the child, laid him aside, and told the household not to tell his father until she did. When Abu Talhah came home and asked about the boy, she said he was calmer than he had been, and she hoped he was at rest. She brought him his supper. They spent the night together. In the morning, she told him. Sahih Muslim's version adds how she told him: she asked, if people lent something to a family and then asked for it back, would the family have the right to refuse? No, he said. Then, she said, seek your reward from God for your son. He went to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and told him everything. The Prophet prayed for blessing on their night together. Readers take this story in different ways. Some see astonishing patience. Some find it hard to read. Both reactions sit honestly with it. What is clear is that Umm Sulaym chose her moment. She let her husband eat and rest before she gave him the news, and she gave it to him in a picture he could hold. A loan, returned.
screen: `IF YOU ACCEPT ISLAM, THAT IS MY DOWRY.` · `THE BOY DIED WHILE HE WAS OUT.` · `HE IS CALMER; I HOPE HE IS AT REST.` · `A LOAN, RETURNED.` · then, large: `FAITH FOR A DOWRY.`

segments.voice: The practice: hold one hard thing gracefully. This one can be gentle. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one hard thing you're carrying right now. Not the hardest. One you can look at. Hold it the way you'd hold something fragile. Breathe in around it. Breathe out, and don't push it away. Ask one question: is there a better moment, or a kinder way, to say what needs saying about it? If you pray, you can say what Muslims say at a loss: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, to God we belong and to Him we return. The bell holds the time.
Umm Sulaym. The mother of Anas, who asked for Islam as her dowry and told her husband of their son's death in a picture of a loan returned. Today's word.
Your line: faith for a dowry. Today, when you have hard news to give, choose the moment and the words with care. Day eight hundred fifty.

howItsDone: Muslims tell Umm Sulaym's story from al-Nasa'i, where her dowry is Abu Talhah's Islam, and from Bukhari and Muslim, where she breaks the news of their son's death; at a loss, Muslims say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.

her picture of the son's death

myth: Umm Sulaym asked Abu Talhah for a large gift of gold
al-Nasa'i says she asked only for his Islam, and nothing else.
she told her husband about their son as soon as he came home
she let him eat and rest, and told him in the morning.
the Prophet prayed for blessing on their night
Bukhari keeps his prayer after Abu Talhah told him.

fork.setup: you are Umm Sulaym. your son has died while your husband was out. he walks in tired and asks how the boy is. what do you do?
options: tell him at once, at the door.
say the boy is calmer, feed him, and tell him in the morning.
send someone else to tell him.
fork.reveal: Bukhari says she said he was calmer and she hoped he was at rest, served supper, and told him in the morning, as a loan returned.

original.note: Arabic: Umm Sulaym, mother of Sulaym, the name she is known by.

trapdoor: what you thought: a story about a mother who hid her grief.
what it means: she chose the moment and the words, and gave her husband a picture he could hold: a loan, returned.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari's version has 'he is calmer'; Muslim's adds the loan question. Readers still argue over how to read her calm.

notes: 'We met a couple of weeks back' refers to Anas ibn Malik on day 838; confirm the link reads well.
Al-Nasa'i 3341 paraphrased ('a man like you is not turned away'); confirm number and wording.
Bukhari 1301/5470 and Muslim 2144 cited from memory; confirm. In Bukhari the boy is unnamed in these reports; the script does not name him.
'Readers take this story in different ways. Some see astonishing patience. Some find it hard to read.' A fair-reading line; Keeper may prefer different wording.

Editor: hook cut 'widow' and 'not a poor man' (not in Nasa'i 3341) and the vague 'a couple of weeks back'; second scene now credited to Bukhari and Muslim, since 'don't tell his father' is Muslim's detail; cut the superlative 'hardest news there is'.
Audit: Muslim 2144's closing words are 'ihtasib ibnak' (seek God's reward for your son), not 'count your son as returned'; corrected. Trapdoor first floor softened from 'a woman with no feelings'.
